string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of China and one of the most important historical and cultural cities in the country. It is located in northern China, where the North China Plain meets hills and mountains. Beijing has served as the capital during several Chinese dynasties and remains the center of national government today. Well-known landmarks include the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven, and sections of the Great Wall near the city. The Forbidden City once housed imperial rulers and is now a major museum. Beijing also has modern universities, business districts, and an extensive subway network.

Shanghai is a major city on China's eastern coast, near the mouth of the Yangtze River. Its development accelerated in the nineteenth century as it became an important trading port. Historic buildings along the Bund reflect this period, while Pudong represents the city's modern growth. Shanghai hosted the World Expo in 2010 and remains a center for business and cultural events. In recent years, it has also welcomed Japanese music performances. Poppin'Party performed at the Oriental Sports Center on August 23, 2025, and MyGO!!!!! and Ave Mujica held joint concerts at the Mercedes-Benz Arena on October 11 and 12, 2025.

Chongqing is a large municipality in southwestern China, situated along the upper reaches of the Yangtze River. Much of its landscape consists of hills, mountains, and deep river valleys. The central city developed where the Yangtze and Jialing rivers meet, creating striking views of bridges and buildings on steep slopes. Chongqing is often called the Mountain City because of its unusual terrain. It is an important transportation and industrial center for inland China. The municipality also includes extensive rural areas beyond its urban districts. Its location makes it a gateway to the Three Gorges region, a well-known stretch of the Yangtze River.

Tianjin is a major city and seaport in northern China, located southeast of Beijing near the Bohai Sea. The Haihe River flows through the city and connects it to coastal waterways. Tianjin has a long history as a transportation and trading center, linking routes between northern and southern China. Its port supports international shipping and business in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region. The city combines modern industry with historic streets and buildings that reflect different periods of development. Visitors can explore areas along the Haihe River and learn about its maritime history. Tianjin is also known for local foods and traditional crafts.
